ai.description: *Hemidactylus vietnamensis* grows to 55 mm SVL. It is grey-brown with dark dorsal blotches and a pale underside. Key features include a slender body, distinct toe pads, and a finely tuberculate back.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemidactylus vietnamensis* is distinguished by its unique, strongly serrated fringe of scales along the sides of the tail, a feature absent in most similar Indian congeners.
ai.habitat: *Hemidactylus vietnamensis* is not found in the Indian subcontinent; it is endemic to the karst limestone forests of northern Vietnam at elevations between 200 and 600 meters.
ai.behavior: The Vietnam leaf-toed gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to actively hunt small insects along rock crevices and tree trunks.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus vietnamensis* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus vietnamensis* is not native to the Indian subcontinent; it is endemic to Vietnam and parts of southern China.
